decision: ACCEPT Peerit release sequence 24 as the LIVE bounded-public-test launch successor: the systemic descriptor-driven admission fix — admission parameterHash is expected from the CURRENT signature-verified descriptor's advertised binding everywhere a client qualifies, never from a release-pinned file — keeping the limited Cell-GET runtime authority EXPOSED at sequence 24 and signed seed recovery ENABLED for the same 34-record live launch seed. The exact production CSP remains unchanged, authenticated browser authority MUST become active before any relay I/O, recovery performs zero network PUTs, ordinary delivery remains LOCAL_ONLY, the all-five successor remains excluded, and the GA product gate remains blocked with all 22 blockers disclosed-open.

authority.owner_instruction: Systemic fix for the rotation class that has now bitten baked-in pins THREE times (descriptor cliffs x3, admission rotations x2). Current live failure on peerit.site (seq-23 deployed): seedRecovery blocked with 'descriptor does not carry the release-signed admission-v3 profile'. Both daemons now run admission-v7; the seq-21/22/23 bundles pin v6-era hashes and fail; the publisher also fails. Clients verify admission against a BAKED-IN parameterHash from build time; the fleet rotates admission on its cadence; every baked pin goes stale within days. Make admission verification DESCRIPTOR-DRIVEN everywhere the client qualifies: derive the expected admission parameterHash from the CURRENT descriptor's admissionProfileBinding (re-probed at runtime), fetch the signed admission parameters where consumed, and verify them against the descriptor's binding. No baked parameterHash anywhere in the qualification path; descriptor signature/chain/admission-parameter signature verification stays exactly as strict — the only change is where the EXPECTED hash comes from (current descriptor, not a file).
